newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds slow down, Russia to tap 10-yr maturity.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds slow down, Russia to tap 10-yr maturity.

text.p: Primary market activity came to a halt on Friday ahead of the week-end.
Issuance was expected to pick up again next week, bankers said, with a number of borrowers eyeing five-year dollars.
Russia's deputy minister of finance Mikhail Kasyanov said at a press conference its forthcoming Eurobond would be for at least $1.0 billion and was expected to have a 10-year maturity.
"On the basis of our analysis of market reception we are looking for a 10-year term and a size of not less than $1.0 billion," Kasyanov, in London to meet investors ahead of the bond, said.
Spread talk on the deal was around 375 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
Russia's other dollar bond, a $1.0 billion five-year launched last November at 345 b.p. over Treasuries, was trading at around 275 b.p. over.
Roadshows for the transaction end on June 18, and launch is expected shortly after.
